fullPassage:
(A) "Mia, let's go walk our dog!" Julia called out, but there was no answer. She checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was absorbed in her smartphone, wearing her earbuds. Julia was concerned about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam. "Mia seems to live inside her phone, not with us." Sam nodded, "I know. I feel like (a) she is growing distant from us. Why don't we set up a family reading club?" Julia brightened at the suggestion, and Sam promised to talk with Mia about it.

(B) Mia's family held their first book club meeting on Saturday afternoon. Everyone enjoyed the book Mia had chosen. Julia was the first to speak: "Dr. Duvall nearly invented a drug for eternal life, yet disappeared one day and ended up running Café Paris. That's such a mystery." Mia responded, her eyes sparkling, "Mom, I understand him. He always dreamed of being a barista, and his dream came true." Sam supported (b) his daughter, and their conversation grew lively. During the discussion, Mia felt reconnected with her parents and already looked forward to their next book club meeting.

(C) At the library, Mia scanned the shelves for nearly an hour, feeling lost among the endless titles. Then, a librarian approached and asked, "Looking for something in particular?" "I need a book for my family's reading club," Mia admitted. "What genre do you enjoy?" she asked kindly. "Hmm, I like mysteries," Mia replied. The librarian handed her a book titled Café Paris and said with a smile, "You'll love this one." Mia thanked (c) her and checked it out.

(D) When Sam suggested starting a family reading club, Mia immediately shook her head and said, "No, Dad. I don't have time to read books. You know how busy (d) I am with exams all semester." He didn't give up. "But wouldn't it be fun if we all read the same story and shared our thoughts? You could simply read for 20 minutes, maybe during your lunch break." After some persuasion, Mia reluctantly agreed. Deep down, (e) she knew she was spending too much time on her phone. So she asked, "Dad, can I choose the first book?" Sam gladly said, "Yes."

questions.passage: Julia was (A)[concerned / delighted] about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam. "Mia seems to live inside her phone, not with us." Sam nodded, "I know. I feel like she is growing (B)[distant / closer] from us. Why don't we set up a family reading (C)[club / class]?"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Julia는 딸에 대해 걱정(concerned)했고, Mia가 점점 멀어지는(distant) 것을 느꼈으며, 가족 독서 클럽(club)을 제안했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① concerned — distant — club: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② delighted(기뻐하는)는 걱정하는 맥락에 부적절
❌ ③ closer(가까워지는)는 distant(멀어지는)의 반의어
❌ ④ class(수업)는 club(클럽)과 다른 의미
det.tip: concerned about(~에 대해 걱정하는), growing distant(점점 멀어지는), reading club(독서 클럽)

det.korean: Mia는 끝없는 책들 사이에서 길을 잃은 듯(lost) 느꼈고, 사서가 다가와서(approached) 물었으며, Mia는 미스터리(mysteries)를 좋아한다고 답했습니다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② excited(흥분한)는 lost(막막한)와 다른 감정
❌ ③ ignored(무시했다)는 approached(다가갔다)의 반의어
❌ ④ comedies(코미디)는 mysteries(미스터리)와 다른 장르
det.tip: feeling lost(막막한 느낌), approach(다가가다), mystery(미스터리 장르)

You could simply read for 20 minutes, maybe during your lunch break." After some (A)[persuasion / hesitation], Mia (B)[reluctantly / eagerly] agreed. Deep down, she knew she was spending too much time on her phone. So she asked, "Dad, can I choose the (C)[first / last] book?"

det.korean: 약간의 설득(persuasion) 끝에 Mia는 마지못해(reluctantly) 동의했고, 첫 번째(first) 책을 자기가 고르겠다고 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ persuasion — reluctantly — first: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ① hesitation(망설임)은 Sam의 설득 행위와 다름
❌ ② eagerly(열성적으로)는 reluctantly(마지못해)의 반의어
❌ ④ last(마지막)는 first(첫 번째)와 반대
det.tip: persuasion(설득) → reluctantly(마지못해) → 점진적 태도 변화 흐름 파악

det.korean: ①distant(멀어지는), ②brightened(밝아졌다), ③promised(약속했다)는 원문과 일치합니다. ④enthusiastically(열정적으로)는 원문의 reluctantly(마지못해)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ enthusiastically(열정적으로) → 원문은 reluctantly(마지못해). Mia가 처음에 거부했다가 마지못해 수락한 맥락
det.tip: reluctantly(마지못해) ↔ enthusiastically(열정적으로): 마지못한 동의라는 맥락 파악이 핵심

questions.passage: Mia's family held their first book club meeting on Saturday afternoon. Everyone ①<u>enjoyed</u> the book Mia had chosen. det.korean: ①enjoyed(즐겼다), ②disappeared(사라졌다), ④reconnected(다시 연결되었다)는 원문과 일치합니다. ③awkward(어색한)는 원문의 lively(활기찬)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②④: 원문 그대로
✅ ③ awkward(어색한) → 원문은 lively(활기찬). 대화가 '어색해진' 것이 아니라 '활발해진' 맥락
det.tip: lively(활기찬) ↔ awkward(어색한): Sam이 딸을 지지하고 대화가 활발해지는 긍정적 흐름

det.korean: ①absorbed(몰두한), ②endless(끝없는), ④looked forward to(기대했다)는 원문과 일치합니다. ③disconnected(단절된)는 원문의 reconnected(다시 연결된)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:

det.tip: reconnected(다시 연결된) ↔ disconnected(단절된): 접두사 re-(다시)와 dis-(분리)의 반대 관계

questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Julia는 Sam의 제안(suggestion)에 표정이 밝아졌습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ suggestion(제안): Sam이 독서 클럽을 '제안'했고 Julia가 반가워함
❌ ① complaint(불평): 제안이지 불평이 아님
❌ ② criticism(비판): 비판적 맥락이 아님
❌ ④ demand(요구): 강압적 요구가 아닌 자연스러운 제안
det.tip: brighten at the suggestion = 제안에 표정이 밝아지다

det.korean: 사서가 Mia에게 어떤 장르(genre)를 좋아하는지 물었고, Mia는 미스터리를 좋아한다고 대답했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ genre(장르): mysteries라는 답변과 자연스럽게 연결
❌ ① author(저자): 답변이 장르명이므로 부적절
❌ ② format(형식): 맥락과 무관
❌ ③ language(언어): 맥락과 무관
det.tip: genre(장르) — mystery, romance, thriller 등 문학 분류

You could simply read for 20 minutes, maybe during your lunch break." After some persuasion, Mia __________ agreed. Deep down, she knew she was spending too much time on her phone. questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 설득 끝에 Mia는 마지못해(reluctantly) 동의했습니다. 처음에 거부했지만 아버지의 설득에 결국 수락한 맥락입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② reluctantly(마지못해): 처음 거부 → 설득 → 마지못한 동의
❌ ① eagerly(열성적으로): 처음 거부한 태도와 모순
❌ ③ immediately(즉시): 설득 과정이 있었으므로 부적절
❌ ④ confidently(자신 있게): 마지못한 동의와 맞지 않음
det.tip: reluctantly = unwillingly = with hesitation: '마지못해' 동의어군

questions.passage: (A) "Mia, let's go walk our dog!" Julia called out, but there was no answer. She checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was <u>absorbed</u> in her smartphone, wearing her earbuds. Julia was concerned about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 absorbed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: absorbed는 '몰두한'이라는 뜻으로, engrossed(몰입한)와 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② engrossed(몰입한) ≈ absorbed(몰두한)
❌ ① bored(지루한): 반의어
❌ ③ confused(혼란스러운): 관련 없음
❌ ④ frightened(겁먹은): 관련 없음
det.tip: absorbed = engrossed = immersed = preoccupied: '몰두한' 동의어군

questions.passage: She checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was absorbed in her smartphone, wearing her earbuds. Julia was <u>concerned</u> about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam. "Mia seems to live inside her phone, not with us." Sam nodded, "I know.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 concerned와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: concerned는 '걱정하는'이라는 뜻으로, worried(걱정하는)와 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① worried(걱정하는) ≈ concerned(걱정하는)
❌ ② satisfied(만족한): 반의어적 뉘앙스
❌ ③ indifferent(무관심한): 걱정의 반대
❌ ④ amused(재미있어하는): 관련 없음
det.tip: concerned = worried = anxious = troubled: '걱정하는' 동의어군

questions.passage: "But wouldn't it be fun if we all read the same story and shared our thoughts? You could simply read for 20 minutes, maybe during your lunch break." After some <u>persuasion</u>, Mia reluctantly agreed. Deep down, (e) she knew she was spending too much time on her phone. So she asked, "Dad, can I choose the first book?" Sam gladly said, "Yes."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 persuasion과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: persuasion은 '설득'이라는 뜻으로, convincing(납득시킴)과 동의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ convincing(납득시킴) ≈ persuasion(설득)
❌ ① punishment(처벌): 관련 없음
❌ ② argument(논쟁): 설득보다 대립적
❌ ③ instruction(지시): 일방적 명령으로 설득과 다름
det.tip: persuasion = convincing = coaxing: '설득' 동의어군. 부드러운 설득 vs 강압의 차이 구분

det.korean: distant는 '멀어지는'이라는 뜻으로, close(가까운)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ close(가까운) ↔ distant(먼)
❌ ① remote(먼): distant의 동의어
❌ ② separate(분리된): distant와 유사
❌ ④ isolated(고립된): distant와 유사
det.tip: distant(먼) ↔ close(가까운): growing distant from us = 우리와 점점 멀어지는

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 reluctantly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: reluctantly는 '마지못해'라는 뜻으로, willingly(기꺼이)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② willingly(기꺼이) ↔ reluctantly(마지못해)
❌ ① hesitantly(머뭇거리며): reluctantly와 유사
❌ ③ grudgingly(불평하며): reluctantly와 유사
❌ ④ cautiously(조심스럽게): 관련 있지만 반의어 아님
det.tip: reluctantly(마지못해) ↔ willingly/eagerly(기꺼이): 태도의 정반대

questions.passage:
(A) At the library, Mia scanned the shelves for nearly an hour. The librarian handed her a book titled Café Paris. Mia thanked her and <u>checked</u> it out.

(B) She <u>checked</u> her daughter's room and found that Mia was absorbed in her smartphone.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 checked가 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A)에서 checked it out은 도서관에서 책을 대출했다, (B)에서 checked her room은 방을 확인했다라는 뜻입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 대출했다 — (B) 확인했다: 각 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ② (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 점검/통제는 두 문맥 모두 부적절
❌ ④ 통제/점검도 문맥 불일치
det.tip: check out = 대출하다(도서관). check = 확인하다(일반). 다의어 check의 문맥별 의미 구분

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"the act of making someone agree to do something by reasoning or arguing"

det.korean: '이유를 들거나 논의하여 누군가를 동의하게 만드는 행위'는 persuasion(설득)의 정의입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ persuasion(설득): 영영풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ① confession(고백): 비밀을 털어놓는 것
❌ ② permission(허가): 허락하는 것
❌ ③ suggestion(제안): 아이디어를 제시하는 것
det.tip: persuasion = the act of persuading. permission(허가)과 혼동 주의 — 어근은 같지만 의미가 다름

questions.passage: Julia was concerned about her daughter. Mia was absorbed in her smartphone. Julia's __________ (concerned) grew as she realized her daughter was growing distant from the family.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: concerned(형용사: 걱정하는) → concern(명사: 걱정). 소유격 Julia's 뒤에 명사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
Julia's + __________ + grew 구조에서 소유격 뒤 명사 필요 → concern
concerned(형) → concern(명/동)
det.tip: concerned(걱정하는, 형) → concern(걱정, 명): 소유격 뒤에는 명사가 위치

questions.passage: Mia immediately shook her head. After some persuasion, Mia reluctantly agreed. She was __________ (reluctance) to join the reading club at first, but eventually came around.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: reluctance(명사: 마지못함) → reluctant(형용사: 마지못하는). be동사 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
was + __________ 구조에서 be동사 뒤 형용사 보어 필요 → reluctant
reluctance(명) → reluctant(형) → reluctantly(부)
det.tip: reluctance(명) → reluctant(형) → reluctantly(부): -ance 명사 → -ant 형용사 변환

❌ ① bored(지루한): 활발한 대화와 모순
❌ ③ frustrated(좌절한): 긍정적 분위기와 불일치
❌ ④ pressured(압박받는): 자발적 즐거움의 맥락과 상반
det.tip: reconnected(다시 연결된): 스마트폰으로 단절 → 독서 클럽으로 재연결이라는 글의 핵심 변화

questions.passage: "Mia, let's go walk our dog!" Julia called out, but there was no answer. She checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was absorbed in her smartphone, wearing her earbuds. Julia was concerned about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam. "Mia seems to live inside her phone, not with us." Sam nodded, "I know. I feel like she is growing distant from us. __________?" Julia brightened at the suggestion, and Sam promised to talk with Mia about it.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Why don't we sign up for a cooking class
Why don't we set up a family reading club
Why don't we limit her screen time
Why don't we take away her phone

det.korean: Sam은 Mia가 멀어지고 있다며 가족 독서 클럽을 만들자(set up a family reading club)고 제안했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ set up a family reading club: 원문 표현 그대로
❌ ① cooking class: 요리 수업은 본문에 없음
❌ ② limit screen time: 직접적이지만 원문의 제안이 아님
❌ ④ take away her phone: 강압적이고 원문과 다름
det.tip: Why don't we~? = ~하는 게 어때? 제안 표현. set up = 설립하다, 만들다
